speech_en: Sugar in the pantry, bile down the gutter!
speech_de: Zucker in die Speisekammer, Galle in die Rinne!
scenario: A chunky many-sided Hepatocyte character in a cook's apron stands in a liver plate doing both of its jobs at once: its left arm reaches over the bank of a wide blood river (with cheerful red blood cells floating past like rubber rings) to catch a tumbling sugar cube, while its right hand tips a watering can of bile into the narrow vertical gutter — the bile canaliculus — that it shares with the neighbouring liver-cell character pressed against its right wall. Short fat finger-bumps (microvilli) line the wall facing the blood, and two big round nuclei show through openings high on its body, because this cell famously has two.
status: RENDERED — accepted on attempt 1 with gemini-3-pro-image. Bleeds off all four edges, no frame/box/margin band, no starburst or radiating rays, no baked-in text, no solid black areas; the trace to SVG produced 250 clean paths. Known cartoon compromise: the two nucleus circles sit high on the body above the character's own face, so at a glance the cell can read as having four eyes — kept because it is the clearest way to show binucleation in a colouring page.
command: uv run --script .claude/skills/microbe-render/scripts/coloring.py --microbe hepatocyte --set epithelial --prompt-file <this prompt> --model gemini-3-pro-image --attempt 1 --speech-en "Sugar in the pantry, bile down the gutter!" --speech-de "Zucker in die Speisekammer, Galle in die Rinne!"
prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) the Hepatocyte must be a CHUNKY MANY-SIDED BLOCK with flat straight walls and blunt angled corners — never a round ball.

SCENE: A cheerful cartoon HEPATOCYTE (liver cell) character stands in the liver between a river of blood on its left and a tiny gutter on its right, doing two jobs at once.
- The HEPATOCYTE is a big, chunky, many-sided block character, like a friendly rounded-off Lego brick or a six-sided garden shed, standing upright in the middle of the picture and filling most of the height. Its front wall carries a BIG FRIENDLY FACE: two large round eyes with pupils, cheerful curved eyebrows, rosy round cheeks and a wide happy open grin. It has two short stubby arms with simple mitten hands and two little stubby feet. It wears a simple cook's apron with a big chunky pocket. Draw a couple of small round window-like openings high on its body through which two big round NUCLEI are visible side by side (this cell famously has TWO), each drawn as a large plain circle with a smaller circle inside it, left completely open so a child can colour them.
- On the LEFT, a wide BLOOD RIVER flows past in a broad open lane that runs off the top and the bottom edge of the picture, drawn with a few long simple wavy current lines and a wall of big simple bricks along its bank with small round holes in them. Three chunky RED BLOOD CELLS float down the river like round rubber rings, each a fat doughnut shape with a simple happy face and tiny waving arms. The Hepatocyte's LEFT arm reaches over the bank and catches a big SUGAR CUBE and a plump round DROPLET tumbling along in the current.
- Along the LEFT WALL of the Hepatocyte, between it and the river, draw a row of short, chunky, finger-like BUMPS of uneven length sticking out, like fat stubby fingers — these are its microvilli. Keep them big and simple, never thin hairs.
- On the RIGHT, a slightly smaller NEIGHBOUR LIVER-CELL character, also a many-sided block with its own simple friendly face and one nucleus circle, stands pressed right up against the Hepatocyte, cut off by the right edge of the picture. Between the two blocks their touching walls leave a NARROW VERTICAL GUTTER, a simple long open channel running from top to bottom of the seam. The Hepatocyte's RIGHT hand tips a chunky watering can so that a few big round DROPS of bile fall into that gutter and flow down it.
- Behind and below, two or three more many-sided liver-cell blocks are stacked to make a wall, running off the bottom and the corners of the picture.
- Everything is drawn LARGE, SIMPLE and CHUNKY, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — the river, the cell blocks and the background elements are CUT OFF by the image edge itself.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — the blood river runs right off the top and bottom edges, the neighbouring cell blocks run off the right, left and bottom edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO blood splashes, no wounds, no scary or angry faces, nothing gruesome.
- NO human figure and no hands other than the characters' own mitten hands.
- NO long wavy hairs, NO fur carpet and NO beating cilia anywhere — the bumps on the cell wall are short fat fingers only.
